text_content: house deputy speaker and antipolo city rep ronnie puno backed senate blue ribbon committee chair ping lacson in maintaining that there is so far no evidence directly linking former speaker ferdinand martin romualdez to the alleged flood control corruption puno said investigations should be guided by evidence and fairness warning against turning serious allegations into political theater in the absence of proof he welcomed lacson's statement that the senate inquiry has not produced sworn testimony or documentary evidence implicating romualdez adding that investigations cannot proceed on conjecture political pressure or unsubstantiated claims in a radio interview lacson said that aside from orly guteza no other witness surfaced to implicate romualdez in the alleged anomalous flood control projects puno also expressed confidence that lacson could not be pressured or dictated on how to conduct the investigation house deputy speaker and la union rep paolo ortega v echoed lacson's position and urged critics to stop applying political pressure after the senator said there was no evidence linking romualdez to the controversy ortega said accountability is important but cannot be built on rumors or unsubstantiated claims adding that the absence of affidavits and documentation leaves no basis for further action lanao del sur rep zia alonto adiong likewise welcomed lacson's statement saying that without factual evidence sworn statements and supporting documents there is nothing to pursue adiong said the allegations raised by guteza remain unsubstantiated and warned that manufacturing allegations without evidence undermines due process he added that public officials are entitled to the same standard of fairness expected of any citizen while romualdez's allies have pointed to the absence of sworn testimony to argue against further proceedings the senate inquiry left several matters outside the official record one unresolved issue involves alleged romualdez bagman sofonias ponyong gabonada who served as house deputy secretary general during romualdez's speakership gabonada was publicly accused by davao del norte governor edwin jubahib of possessing unexplained wealth far beyond what could be justified by his reported php 200,000 monthly salary as a house official jubahib alleged that gabonada owns a php 30 million house in tagum city filled with luxury vehicles a php 50 million beach resort in davao de oro and heavy equipment valued at more than php 200 million senator ronald dela rosa said during one senate hearing that gabonada should be summoned to testify but gabonada was never ordered to appear before the senate another aspect of the inquiry involved allegations that members of the so-called bulacan group of contractors bgc laundered flood control funds through casinos in a privilege speech lacson cited information obtained from pagcor regarding large casino transactions allegedly involving the group despite these claims the lacson-led blue ribbon committee did not summon casino representatives to testify the hearings did not include sworn testimony from casino operators regarding the alleged use of fake names and ids or the reported conversion of cash into chips later declared as winnings as alleged by lacson puno meanwhile is a senior leader of the national unity party he previously initiated an ethics complaint against cavite rep kiko barzaga a fellow nup member and vocal critic of romualdez following barzaga's public allegations of corruption puno is one of the names emerging amid ongoing maneuvering to unseat house speaker bojie dy the senate blue ribbon committee hearing on the flood control corruption controversy is scheduled to resume on january 19 according to lacson

text_content: proclamation no 3 series of 2024 declaring the suspension of classes in all levels of public and private schools and the adoption of work-from-home arrangement in government offices in davao city on friday january 19 2024 due to heavy rains brought about by the shear line weather system whereas at 8:00 pm of january 18 2024 the department of science and technology philippine atmospheric geophysical and astronomical services administration dost-pagasa mindanao regional services division mprsd issued heavy rainfall warning number 5 due to the shear line continuing to affect the region at the yellow warning level with possible flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in mountainous areas whereas the same advisory indicates that moderate to occasionally heavy rains 4.5-7.5 with occasionally 7.5-15 liters/meter 2 per hour are being experienced in identified areas in mindanao including davao city whereas at 7:30 pm of january 18 2024 the pagasa davao river basin flood forecasting and warning center issued flood advisory no 1 a indicating various rivers in the city at critical and alert levels with the davao river and its tributaries particularly salug matupe kiulom tagaulay sita dumalogdog simud ipuan gumitan upian kulafu suawan siao and tamugan rivers as areas of concern whereas with the continued moderate to heavy rainfall in the city causing increasing water levels at various rivers and flooding in certain streets the davao city disaster risk reduction davao city disaster risk reduction and management office has called for preemptive and mandatory evacuations in many areas in the city whereas the city government of davao is duty-bound to safeguard the welfare of the public and undertake measures to avert any untoward incidents or disasters that may be caused by the effects of said weather occurrence now therefore i sebastian z duterte mayor of the city of davao by virtue of the powers vested in me by law do hereby declare the following to take effect on friday january 19 2024:1 that classes and school activities in all levels in all public and private educational institutions in davao city are hereby suspended 2 that the work-from-home wfh arrangement shall be adopted in all national and local government offices including government-owned and controlled corporations in davao city except for offices performing safety and security health social services and disaster and emergency response services and 3 that private offices and establishments are given the discretion to suspend work or adopt wfh arrangements but are encouraged to do so for the safety and convenience of their employees done this 18th day of january 2024 in davao city philippines source city government of davao

text_content: engineering a flood-resilient davao a look into the jica flood control master plan davao city's rapid urban growth and unique geography make flood management a complex critical challenge tackling water-induced hazards requires more than just reactive measures-it demands a science-backed basin-wide hydrological strategy the department of public works and highways dpwh in partnership with the japan international cooperation agency jica developed the master plan and feasibility study on flood control and drainage in davao city here is a bird's-eye view of how this comprehensive framework aims to protect our communities 1 broad scope across 3 major basins flooding isn't isolated to one river the master plan covers a massive 2,200 km2 target area addressing three distinct flood types-riverine inland urban drainage and coastal-across three key river basins davao river basin 1,755 km2 talomo river basin 204 km2 matina river basin 70 km2 2 structural interventions hard engineering to physically manage extreme peak flows during heavy weather events major infrastructure upgrades are proposed retarding ponds large detention basins to temporarily store stormwater and shave off peak flood flows downstream river dredging deepening critical channel beds to maximize volumetric flow capacity cut-off channels and floodwalls realignment works including a cut-off-works cum bridge to bypass tight meanders and safely contain floodwaters urban drainage upgrades re-engineering internal city networks to prevent localized pooling 3 non-structural measures policy and preparedness infrastructure alone cannot eliminate risk the plan heavily integrates non-structural controls telemetry and early warning real-time forecasting systems to provide crucial lead time for communities land-use and zoning controls restricting high-density development in active natural floodplains community preparedness targeted evacuation and safety protocols for vulnerable areas like bucana ma-a waan and mandug 4 geotechnical and environmental controls a key engineering hurdle identified is managing the massive volume of excavated silt and soil without strict geotechnical protocols-such as temporary siltation ponds and silt curtains-dredging operations risk causing severe downstream sedimentation in the davao river and davao gulf engineering long-term flood resilience requires a balance of heavy civil solutions environmental safeguards and proactive community planning stay tuned as we break down each of these four areas in our upcoming deep-dive posts davao city
